A user says they long ago gave up traditional desktop streaming tools like TeamViewer/AnyDesk for game streaming software (Parsec, Rainway, Steam Remote Play). They find its streaming tech 'worlds ahead' in quality, efficiency, stability and latency, with better onboarding and UX. They see no reason to use the traditional players for personal use.
A commenter notes that TeamViewer/AnyDesk regularly take action to disable accounts used by fake tech-support scam call centers. They cite YouTube channels like Jim Browning and Kitboga as examples.

On AnyDesk's response to the 2024 hack (resetting passwords, revoking certificates, saying it is 'safe to use AnyDesk'), a commenter criticized the lack of answers. If they were a customer, they would want more details on what actually happened before using the software again.
A user says they were about to recommend AnyDesk to their employer after several bad experiences with TeamViewer. The hack news gave them pause.
A commenter's perception of AnyDesk: 'I thought that was just a tool used by India-based scammers to access old people's computers.'
Criticism of the timing of AnyDesk's breach disclosure: 'Page 1 of the IR playbook, announce it Friday evening.'

A user doing occasional remote support for a club's Win10 machine from Linux moved from LogMeIn to TeamViewer (which also got breached) to AnyDesk. After the AnyDesk breach, they are considering Tailscale + RDP instead, but need unattended access with no interaction at the remote end.
On AnyDesk's launch: 'Did I miss the Mac version or is that not available? Show-stopper for just about everyone I know.'
A user complained that the AnyDesk website broke normal mouse-wheel scrolling.

A commenter criticized AnyDesk's launch benchmark: the framerate graph didn't seem to match the data in the benchmark PDF. They also asked why the RDP version wasn't listed (RDP 8.0 brought a big quality bump) and why paid competitors weren't included.
A user pointed out a Polish translation error on AnyDesk's site: 'Latency' was rendered as 'Latencja' (a viral incubation period) instead of 'Opóźnienie'.

A user suggested the free Brynhildr instead of AnyDesk for '60fps for free'. They said AnyDesk isn't for them because they expect a remote tool to show port numbers, bandwidth use and codec, 'not treat me like an idiot'.
